stories.title: Danshensu attenuates type 2 diabetes-related osteoporosis via the PI3K/AKT/Nrf2 signaling pathway
stories.description: Danshensu (DSS), a water-soluble phenolic acid derived from Salvia miltiorrhiza, exhibits antioxidant and osteoprotective properties; however, its effects on type 2 diabetes-related osteoporosis (T2DOP) have not been fully defined. We therefore evaluated the effects of DSS on T2DOP and examined whether PI3K/AKT/Nrf2 signaling participates in its actions. Potential molecular targets and signaling pathways associated with DSS were first screened through a network pharmacology approach. In vivo, T2DOP was induced in mice by high-fat feeding followed by low-dose streptozotocin administration; in parallel, high-glucose-exposed BMSCs served as the cellular model. DSS improved trabecular bone microarchitecture and alleviated bone loss in T2DOP mice. In high-glucose-treated BMSCs, DSS reduced ROS and MDA levels, enhanced SOD and CAT activities, and preserved osteogenic capacity, with higher ALP activity, greater mineralized nodule formation, and increased expression of osteogenesis-related markers. DSS treatment was also accompanied by enhanced PI3K and AKT phosphorylation together with higher Nrf2 expression. Blocking either PI3K or Nrf2 pharmacologically weakened the DSS-induced responses. Collectively, DSS appears to counter T2DOP partly by engaging PI3K/AKT/Nrf2-related antioxidant responses and maintaining osteogenic differentiation.

stories.title: Factors associated with surgical outcomes following maxillomandibular advancement for obstructive sleep apnea: a systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis
stories.description: Maxillomandibular advancement (MMA) is one of the most effective surgical treatments for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but treatment response varies considerably among patients. We performed a systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis to evaluate factors associated with treatment response following MMA. The review protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251274643). PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and the Cochrane Library were searched for observational studies reporting postoperative outcomes together with factors associated with surgical response. Study quality was assessed using the ROBINS-I tool. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed when studies were sufficiently comparable; otherwise, findings were synthesized narratively. Thirteen studies met the inclusion criteria. Definitions of surgical success varied substantially across studies, although most used the Sher criteria or postoperative apnea–hypopnea index thresholds. Across six independent cohorts, the random-effects pooled surgical success rate was 70.7% (95% CI, 62.5%–77.7%), although this estimate should be interpreted cautiously because of methodological heterogeneity. Younger age, lower central apnea burden, and favorable cephalometric and upper airway characteristics were more consistently associated with improved treatment response, whereas evidence for body mass index, sex, baseline disease severity, and the magnitude of skeletal advancement was inconsistent. These findings support comprehensive patient selection integrating clinical, polysomnographic, and anatomical characteristics and underscore the need for prospective studies using standardized outcome definitions and validated prediction models.
